rationale: The buyer is a solo indie animator/video creator — a consumer-adjacent prosumer who has demonstrated spend ($75 on a voice actor plus an ElevenLabs subscription), so willingness to pay is real but modest. The segment is narrow and the individual unit economics are low (one-off project spend rather than recurring B2B budget), and buyer_clarity sits below the build_gate floor of 6. More critically, operational_autonomy is constrained: producing truly consistent, emotionally coherent multi-line character voices still requires per-job human quality review and iteration, meaning delivery is not yet fully automatable at a quality bar that beats ElevenLabs. The deciding factor is that the underlying TTS differentiation is a hard technical problem — without proprietary model-fine-tuning or a clear API wrapper that solves the consistency gap, this is a thin wrapper on commodity tools that won't retain users.
solution_plan: The micro-service would be a 'Character Voice Pack' batch processor: a user submits a character description, a short reference clip, and up to 50 lines of script via a web form; Claude orchestrates calls to a premium TTS API (e.g. ElevenLabs v3 or PlayHT) with a locked voice profile and emotion-tagged prompts, then delivers a ZIP of rendered audio files. BUILD: the factory sets up a simple intake form (Tally or Typeform), a Claude orchestration prompt that injects character consistency metadata into each TTS API call, and a Stripe payment link for a per-pack fee (e.g. $15–$25 for 50 lines). No coding by Youval. SELL: reach indie animators on Reddit (r/animation, r/learnanimation), Bluesky animation communities, and itch.io forums — outreach copy prepared by the factory, sent only after Youval approves each batch. MAINTAIN: Claude handles TTS API calls, file packaging, and email delivery of the ZIP; Stripe handles billing; the only recurring human step is approving outreach batches and reviewing the occasional support ticket. CAVEAT: the quality ceiling is set by the underlying TTS APIs, which are the same tools the buyer already tried — without a meaningful consistency improvement over raw ElevenLabs, retention will be very low, and this is the honest blocker to building.
notes: build_gates not met: buyer_clarity = 5 (below floor of 6 — indie animators are a consumer-adjacent prosumer segment with limited recurring budget and high price sensitivity); operational_autonomy = 5 (below floor of 7 — per-job quality review and iteration make fully automated delivery unreliable at a quality bar above existing tools). Validate by testing whether a small cohort of indie animators will pay $15–$25 per batch AND rate output quality meaningfully above ElevenLabs before committing to build.
